---
title: Icon themes
description: File and folder icons, in VS Code's icon theme format.
icon: Shapes
---

An icon theme decides which icon each file and folder gets. It is a separate track from the color theme, with its own picker: press <Kbd>⌘,</Kbd> and choose **Icons**.

Atlas uses VS Code's `iconThemes` contribution format, unchanged. An icon theme published for VS Code installs here as it is, with no conversion step and no Atlas-specific format to learn.

## Pick one

The picker opens on a preview strip and a grid of what is installed. Every card names the theme, its author, and its license.

Three kinds of entry:

- **Material Icon Theme**, bundled with Atlas and selected on a fresh install. Version 5.38.1, MIT licensed, shipped whole with its license and a provenance note.
- **Minimal**, which is not an empty icon theme but no icon theme. Every row falls back to the lucide icon Atlas drew before icon themes existed.
- Anything you installed, marked **Installed** and removable.

Your choice is stored in `~/.config/atlas/config.toml`:

```toml title="~/.config/atlas/config.toml"
[settings]
iconTheme = "material-icon-theme"   # or "minimal", or an installed id
```

The value names a directory, so it is restricted to letters, digits, `.`, `-`, and `_`. Anything else is refused when the config is read.

## Where icons appear

The file tree, the editor tab strip for tabs opened from a path, and the file-search palette on <Kbd>⌘P</Kbd>.

Rows that do not stand for a real path, such as a knowledge page or a chat, keep their own icons.

## Install from Open VSX

Open VSX is the one remote source Atlas has for icons, at the bottom of the **Icons** page. Type a query, press Enter, and pick a result.

Search results are filtered on each candidate's own manifest, so a theme appears only if it actually declares `contributes.iconThemes`. Color themes do not clutter the list.

A `.vsix` is a zip. Atlas unpacks only its `extension/` subtree, checks every entry for path traversal, and stages the result in a temporary directory that is swapped into place only once it loads as an icon theme. A failed install leaves what you had.

Installed themes live in `~/.config/atlas/icon-themes/<namespace>.<name>/`, so Material installed from Open VSX would be `PKief.material-icon-theme`.

<Callout type="info">
  Nothing is fetched at startup or on a timer. Every request Atlas makes to Open VSX is one you asked for by clicking. Being offline costs you a search, not a launch: the failure is reported in place with a retry, and the installed list is untouched.
</Callout>

**To remove one**, hover its card and click the bin. Bundled entries and Minimal have no bin. If you remove the theme that is currently selected, Atlas falls back to Material.

Installing, removing, and switching all take effect immediately. Every visible icon re-resolves with no reload.

## How a theme decides

Everything below is VS Code's format, not Atlas's. The authority is the theme document named by `contributes.iconThemes[0].path` in the extension manifest.

### Definitions

`iconDefinitions` maps an id to an icon, which is either an image or a font glyph:

```json
{
  "iconDefinitions": {
    "typescript": { "iconPath": "./../icons/typescript.svg" },
    "_seti_ts": {
      "fontCharacter": "\\E001",
      "fontColor": "#519aba",
      "fontSize": "150%",
      "fontId": "seti"
    }
  }
}
```

`iconPath` is relative to the theme document, and `.` and `..` are resolved. SVG and PNG both work. When a definition sets both, `iconPath` wins.

Glyph themes declare their web fonts in a `fonts` array. Atlas reads the font file and hands it to the interface inline, so the font loads without any file access, and it is fetched only once a glyph icon has actually been resolved. An SVG-only theme never loads one.

### Associations

| Key | Matches |
|---|---|
| `file` | any file with no better answer |
| `folder`, `folderExpanded` | any folder, closed or open |
| `rootFolder`, `rootFolderExpanded` | the project root |
| `fileNames` | a whole file name, optionally prefixed with its parent path |
| `fileExtensions` | an extension, case-insensitively |
| `languageIds` | the editor's language id for the file |
| `folderNames`, `folderNamesExpanded` | a folder name, optionally prefixed |
| `rootFolderNames`, `rootFolderNamesExpanded` | the root folder by name |

A `light` and a `highContrast` section may override any of those tables. Both are partial: a key the section does not set falls through to the base set. The light section is used when the color theme resolves to a light appearance, and high contrast falls back to the base set rather than to light, since the two are siblings.

`hidesExplorerArrows` is honoured. A theme whose folder icons already say open or closed can ask the file tree to drop its chevrons, and the indent spacer stays so names still line up.

### Precedence

For a file, first hit wins:

1. `fileNames`
2. `fileExtensions`
3. `languageIds`
4. `file`

For a folder, `folderNamesExpanded` when open, then `folderNames`, then `folderExpanded` or `folder`. For the root, the `rootFolder*` family first, falling back to the folder family.

Two rules cut across all of it.

**A parent-path-prefixed entry beats a bare one.** `.config/graphqlrc` wins over `graphqlrc`, and `.github/workflows` over `workflows`. Up to four path segments are considered. Material ships 204 prefixed file names and 25 prefixed folder names, so this decides a lot of rows.

**The longest extension wins.** `types.d.ts` gets the `d.ts` icon, not the `ts` one. A dotfile's name is never read as an extension: `.gitignore` has a name, not an extension.

The `light` or `highContrast` table is consulted at each step, not once for the whole chain. Otherwise a `light.fileExtensions` hit would beat a base `fileNames` hit, which inverts the order above for every theme whose light section is partial, and they all are.

`languageIds` is matched against the editor's own language id for the path. There is no second language table, so a file the editor calls `rust` is the file a theme's `"rust"` entry matches. A path the editor cannot identify sends no language id at all.

### Color

Where a theme sets color, the theme wins. A glyph's `fontColor` is used as written, and an SVG's own `fill` values are drawn as authored, which is how all 1,251 Material icons paint.

Where a theme leaves color open, your color theme supplies it. Atlas inlines SVG icons rather than pointing an `<img>` at them precisely so that an icon drawn in `currentColor` inherits the row's color and follows the active theme. The Minimal fallbacks are Atlas's own icons and always follow the theme.

Inlining third-party markup means every icon is sanitised first, against a drawing-only element allowlist, with no event handlers, no external references, and no `<style>`. An icon that does not survive that pass keeps its lucide fallback rather than rendering an empty box.

## Limits

Atlas reads part of the VS Code format rather than all of it. These limits are known and deliberate, and none of them stop a theme from loading: an affected icon falls back rather than breaking.

<Mermaid chart={`
flowchart LR
    subgraph V["the VS Code icon theme format"]
        direction LR
        I["what Atlas reads<br/>icon definitions, file and folder<br/>rules, light and high contrast"]
        X["not read<br/>product icons, translations,<br/>unsafe SVG elements"]
        I ~~~ X
    end
    I ==>|"nothing matches"| L["the lucide icon"]
    X -.-> L
`} />

- **`<style>` elements inside an icon** are removed. CSS inside an inline SVG is document-scoped and would escape the icon.
- **External references inside an icon** are removed for the same reason.
- **`foreignObject` and embedded raster `<image>` elements** are not on the drawing allowlist.
- **Product icon themes** (`contributes.productIconThemes`) are not read. An extension that contributes only a product icon theme is filtered out of search and refused at install.
- **More than one icon theme per extension.** The first `contributes.iconThemes` entry is the one used.
- **`showLanguageModeIcons`** is parsed and ignored. It controls a status-bar affordance Atlas does not have.
- **Theme-supplied localisation** (`package.nls.*.json`) is not read. A theme's display name is shown as published, untranslated.
- **Editing an installed theme's files in place** needs a restart. Color themes watch `~/.config/atlas/themes/`; icon themes do not watch their directory. Installing and removing refresh the list.
- **Nothing outside the icon theme is taken from a `.vsix`.** The compiled extension host, its commands, and its settings are dropped on unpack. Atlas does not run extensions.
